question.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})⟩,\,0\le s<10\pi .
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}))⟩ \\  & =⟨-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})\cdot \frac{1}{5},\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})\cdot \frac{1}{5}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}))⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})\cdot \frac{1}{5},\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})\cdot \frac{1}{5}⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|-\frac{1}{5}|\sqrt{{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
